About the New Venture Challenge (NVC)
The New Venture Challenge (NVC) – a signature program of the University of Colorado Boulder's Innovation & Entrepreneurship Initiative — is a launchpad for aspiring problem-solvers and creatives. During this multi-round, multi-event entrepreneurial competition, teams can win a share of $320,000 and pitch to a live audience at the Boulder Theater. Learn More

 

Who can participate?

Everyone at CU Boulder is invited to participate – current students, faculty, staff or recent graduates. NVC participants can earn a microcredential while gaining experience in creating a startup venture.

 

How Does it Work?

Participants can compete in one of two NVC categories:

Deep Tech Category – for ventures built around a scientific or technological innovation that has been developed using fundamental scientific disciplinesOpen Category – for ventures not meeting the Deep Tech criteria 

Specialty Competition Opportunities

Additionally, NVC offers two specialty competition opportunities:

Social Impact New Venture Challenge – for ventures that want to create a positive social impactWomen Founders Competition – for teams with at least one core team member who is a woman

title: Anniversary Open House at the Mountain Research Station - University of Colorado Boulder
description:
Celebrate the Mountain Research Station’s 106th anniversary and INSTAAR's 75th at our scenic field science outpost in the Indian Peaks.

 



 

Calling all science lovers! The Open House at the Mountain Research Station is your chance to visit Colorado's premier alpine field science facility, run by INSTAAR. The day will feature guided field trips, hands-on activities, dinner, and a keynote from eminent ecologist Katharine Suding. You can come for one session only or stay for the whole day. Tickets are limited, so be sure to reserve tickets for each session you’d like to join.

 

2026 is the 150th anniversary of CU Boulder, the 75th anniversary of the Institute of Arctic and Alpine Research (INSTAAR), and the 106th anniversary of the Mountain Research Station (MRS). Come celebrate with us!

 

This event is supported by INSTAAR and was partially funded through a grant from the 150th Initiative Fund. If you are able, please consider making a donation to help offset the remaining event costs and support INSTAAR and the Mountain Research Station. You can also donate to the Niwot Ridge Long Term Ecological Research Program via the NWT-LTER giving page.

 

----------------------------------------
Many activities to choose from

Space is limited for all activities except the Field Science Fair and self-guided interpretive trails (both 2-6 pm), so be sure to reserve tickets for each session you’d like to join. 

 

Reserve your tickets with Eventbrite >

 

07:45 AM - 01:00 PM
Hike to Niwot Ridge
Dr. Nancy Emery, Dr. Scott Taylor
The Niwot Ridge Long-Term Ecological Research site is the home to one of the world's premier alpine research programs, with a legacy that spans decades of continuous scientific inquiry. This strenuous hike will begin with a 30-minute drive up a rugged mountain road, followed by a 1.5-mile hike gaining 1,000 feet over steep, rocky terrain. Program scientists will guide attendees through the ridge's core research area, offering an inside look at the instruments and experiments behind key long term inquiries in the alpine.

 

02:00 PM - 06:00 PM
Field Science Fair
Reservations not needed, just walk on in
Join researchers in the Kiowa Classroom and Lab for an interactive, come and go, showcase of field science at the MRS. Researchers will share field equipment, samples, specimens, and more, covering a diverse set of topics including insects, biogeochemistry, plant evolution, alpine lake ecology, bird biology, and mammalogy.

 

02:00 PM - 06:00 PM
Self-guided interpretive trails
Reservations not needed, just start walking
Explore our three self-guided interpretive trails on your own. The trails are short, roughly 1/4 to 1/3 mile long and have interpretive signs in key areas along the trail. Key rules: foot traffic only, stay on trail, no dogs, and no bicycles. 

Trail 1: Como Creek / Riparian Zone. Learn about forest diversity, hydrology and aquatic ecology, our geomorphic setting, and our high-mountain watershed.

Trail 2: Subalpine Forest. Learn about our dynamic forests, biological interactions, and mammals— including how to identify their tracks and scat.

Trail 3: Research at the MRS. Learn about environmental monitoring, long-term data sets collected on Niwot Ridge, and the history of monitoring on Niwot Ridge.

 

02:00 PM - 04:00 PM
Hike to C1
Dr. Sara Hart, Dr. Keith Musselman, Jen Morse
Catch a glimpse into long term monitoring at the MRS. C1 is a subalpine climate station established along a monitoring transect in 1951. This is a moderately strenuous hike (3 miles round trip) that starts and ends at the Marr Lab (9500 feet), highlighted by a mid-hike tour of C1 (10,000 feet), a SNOTEL site, and the Eco Tram project. Along the way, you'll stop and discuss the long-term forest plots that have been monitored since the 1980's.

 

02:00 PM - 03:30 PM
MRS campus tour 1
Lucas Florsheim, Nathaniel Neal
Learn about the history of the MRS on a tour of the facilities, housing, Como Creek, and Elk Meadows. This easy to moderate hike will stay within the CU-Boulder owned Columbine Spring Reserve. The final ascent to Elk Meadows involves a narrow and steep rocky trail.

 

03:00 PM - 04:30 PM
MRS campus tour 2
Dr. Scott Taylor
Learn about the history of the MRS on a tour of the facilities, housing, Como Creek, and Elk Meadows. This easy to moderate hike will stay within the CU-Boulder owned Columbine Spring Reserve. The final ascent to Elk Meadows involves a narrow and steep rocky trail.

 

04:00 PM - 05:30 PM
MRS campus tour 3
Lucas Florsheim, Nathaniel Neal
Learn about the history of the MRS on a tour of the facilities, housing, Como Creek, and Elk Meadows. This easy to moderate hike will stay within the CU-Boulder owned Columbine Spring Reserve. The final ascent to Elk Meadows involves a narrow and steep rocky trail.

 

06:00 PM - 07:00 PM
Dinner
Enjoy a catered dinner at the MRS dining hall. Chat with other science lovers and INSTAAR faculty over hearty local fare from Kathmandu Restaurant.

 

07:00 PM - 08:00 PM
Keynote with Dr. Katharine Suding
Dr. Katharine Suding
Enjoy a keynote seminar from ecologist Katharine Suding in the historic Megaron building. Katharine Suding is a plant community ecologist, the former principal investigator of the Niwot Ridge LTER, and the recipient of the Franklin Institute Bower award in science.

 

Reserve your tickets with Eventbrite >

 

----------------------------------------
Map of the station campus



 

----------------------------------------
Park nearby and use the free shuttle 

Open House parking is extremely limited at the station.  Set your mapping app to park at the South Sourdough Trailhead instead (115 Colorado Road 116).

 

From the trailhead, hop on the free shuttle 0.7 mile to the station.  Thanks!

 

 

----------------------------------------
Frequently asked questions

 

Is this event accessible?
There will be a free shuttle between all event locations throughout the day, so no walking is required for non-hiking events. Please reach out to station manager Michael Haffey (mhaffey@colorado.edu) for accommodations or station director Scott Taylor (scott.a.taylor@colorado.edu) with questions.

 

How do I get to the MRS?
Our main parking area for this event is the South Sourdough Trailhead (115 Colorado Road 116), just down the road from the Mountain Research Station. There you can pick up a free shuttle to the event. The trailhead is a 40-minute drive from Boulder. Please drive slow and watch out for wildlife on the final stretch of dirt road!

 

What should I bring to the MRS open house?
No matter which activity you sign up for, be sure to bring water, extra clothing, a rain coat and sun protection. If you sign up for one of our hikes, you will get an email with further guidance.

 

Can I bring my dog to the MRS?
No. We love our dogs too, but please leave your dogs at home for all MRS open house events unless they are designated service animals.

 

----------------------------------------
Please consider donating

We are able to make this a FREE event thanks to partial funding from the CU Boulder 150th Initiative Fund. But if you are able, we would greatly appreciate a donation to help offset our remaining event costs, feed the grad student volunteers assisting the event, and generally support our research, education, and outreach.  Your options:

INSTAAR givingMountain Research Station givingNiwot Ridge Long Term Ecological Research Program giving

title: Crucial Influence: Leadership Skills for Behavior Change - University of Colorado Boulder
description:
Course Description

When facing persistent, resistant challenges, leaders often surrender to poor results or invest in change efforts that waste time and resources. And yet it’s possible to influence behavior with surprisingly predictable success. For the past thirty years, we’ve studied leaders with a proven ability to influence rapid, profound and sustainable change. And here’s what we know: human behavior is grounded in six sources of influence. Effective leaders know how to leverage and apply these sources of influence to solve everyday leadership challenges.

Crucial Influence® teaches leadership skills that are essential to leaders at every level. Drawing on five decades of social science research and work with successful leaders around the world, the Crucial Influence Model reveals why people do what they do and how all leaders—from aspiring leaders to top executives—can influence others for lasting results.

Crucial Influence incorporates group discussion, video case studies, personal reflection, and engaging exercises into an active learning experience that enables learners to develop an influence plan to solve their challenges.
 

Learning Outcomes

Identify the influence challenges you face as a leader that are keeping you from results.Clarify the vital behaviors that directly drive results.Examine the Six Sources of Influence - personal, social, and structural factors - to discover the causes of any behavior.Diagnose why the current behavior exists to prescribe the most effective and comprehensive solution.Learn how to engage multiple sources of influence to overwhelm persistent and resistent behaviors.Help others want to do vital behaviors by connecting to values.Invest in deliberative practice to significantly enhance personal ability.Harness the power of social influence.Identify and engage opinion leaders.Make incentives and consequences work for you by supporting, not undermining, desired behaviors.Change the environment to make bad behaviors harder and good behaviors easier.Practice using all the skills of Crucial Influence on a real-life case.Make plans to execute on your own Influence Challenge plan.
 Who should attend
Crucial Influence is appropriate for leaders at every level of the organization.

title: Campus Life: 150 Years of Human and More-Than-Human Relationships at CU Boulder Exhibition - University of Colorado Boulder
description:
Campus Life explores the shared history of humans and more-than-human inhabitants over the 150 years of CU Boulder, documenting their evolving relationship. The works exhibited illustrate how different forms of life coexist on campus through a diverse collection of visual media including historical maps, photographs, original watercolors and modern cartography that tracks current and past human-wildlife interactions. 

 

As part of the exhibition, the curators are collecting oral stories from peoples' experiences with the more-than-human on and around campus. Contribute your personal experience to the project.

 

Visitors are also invited to enter the Campus Life Trivia Contest while exploring the exhibit to be eligible for a prize drawing. Follow the gingko leaves and respond to the questions to win a photo or a $50 dollar Amazon gift card.

 

Campus Life is a collaboration with NEST Studio for the Arts, the Museum of Natural History and Facilities Management.

 

The exhibition is on view until December 2026. Please check the Univeristy Libraries hours page for any exceptions.

title: Innovation Workshop Series: Prototyping - University of Colorado Boulder
description:
You're going to build something with your own two hands, and learn how the process we teach you is infinitely translatable!

 

Prototyping is less about building and more about developing your idea by asking the right questions. What is this going to look like? How will it work for a user? This applies for software, hardware, processes, and everything in between.

 

In this workshop, you’ll get another tool in your problem-solving toolbox: how to develop your idea. You’re going to build something with your own two hands, and learn how the process we teach you is infinitely translatable to your next startup idea or in your next job. No previous experience needed. This workshop is useful to anyone with big (or small!) ideas!

 

In each session of the Innovation Workshop Series, you’ll work with a professional who’s an expert in the field, from prototyping to storytelling. You can drop into any one workshop or attend them all—think of it like choosing which tools you need for problem-solving. Whether you want to build keg-powered bikes in your garage or learn some of the skills you’ll need to set yourself apart when you’re applying for jobs, we invite you to come build cool stuff with us in these sandbox-style workshops., powered by Localist Event Calendar Software

title: Sustainability on Tap with Eve Hinckley and Danielle Beatty! - University of Colorado Boulder
description:
Sustainability on Tap
Upslope Brewing Company (East Boulder)
Wednesday, May 20th

Hosted by the Sustainability Research Initiative (SRI), Sustainability on Tap is a monthly conversation series that brings sustainability research out of the classroom and into the community. Held this month at Upslope Brewing Company (East Boulder), the event creates a relaxed, welcoming space for dialogue, curiosity, and connection with the broader Boulder community.

Rather than a traditional academic lecture, this series is designed to feel like a conversation: thought provoking, accessible, and grounded in real world impact. Each month features researchers and practitioners sharing ideas that connect complex research to everyday life.

This Month's Featured Speakers:

Eve Hinckley: Biogeochemist and lead of the Environmental Biogeochemistry Group, Eve-Lyn studies how human activity alters the fundamental processes of life on Earth. From California croplands to the peaks of Patagonia, her team uses isotope geochemistry and data analysis to track the health of fragile ecosystems. She is also a dedicated advocate for diversifying STEM education and mentoring undergraduate researchers.Danielle Beatty: A graduate researcher in the Living Materials Laboratory, Danielle focuses on using microorganisms to grow sustainable, biologically derived building materials. Her work aims to reduce the environmental footprint of the construction industry by reimagining materials design—from raw sourcing to end-of-life reuse.Join us for an informal evening of discussion over drinks, where you can engage directly with the people doing meaningful sustainability work at CU Boulder and beyond. Whether you’re deeply immersed in sustainability research or simply curious, come spark a new connection!, powered by Localist Event Calendar Software

title: PhET founder and Nobel laureate Carl Wieman awarded $4 million Yidan Prize for Education Research | Innovation & Entrepreneurship Initiative

description: OnKure, a privately-held biopharmaceutical company developing best-in-class, targeted oncology therapeutics, announced that it has raised $55 million in a Series B financing. Proceeds will be used to advance the Company’s next generation histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors further into clinical development and fund a growing pipeline of earlier stage molecules.

title: Expect fungi-based steak on your plate by 2022: CU Boulder spinout Meati raises $50 million | Innovation & Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: Meati uses the roots of mushrooms to produce whole cuts, like steak ready to slice on top of a salad or chicken breast breaded and fried as a sandwich. Much of the funds from its recent Series B will go toward completing construction on an 80,000-square-foot production plant, which will soon pump out millions of pounds of Meati in time for a commercial launch in 2022. Meati was founded in 2019 by Huggins and CTO Justin Whiteley, after meeting at CU Boulder while working toward their own PhDs.

title: Startup Colorado Hits 1,000 Members on Entrepreneur Network - Startup Colorado
description: Two years ago, the Startup Colorado Network began as a series of conversations between our small, but mighty team and our rural partners throughout the state. The world was turned upside down and we sensed a heightened need for connectivity, cohesion of resources, and a space for entrepreneurs to build community. After months of research, surveys, and meetings, the Startup Colorado team came to the conclusion that an online network for entrepreneurs would help solve these problems. There was just one big question: if we build it, would they come?

title: Startup Colorado Announces First Founder CO-OPetition Cohort - Startup Colorado
description: In the fall of 2021, Startup Colorado launched a free CO-OPetition pilot program for idea to early stage entrepreneurs. Merging the concepts of “cooperation” and “competition,” the four-week experience invited entrepreneurs to participate in weekly activities by not only building their own business, but also providing feedback for others. At the end of the program, participants anonymously evaluated and voted for a winner. Startup Colorado provided $15,000 in funding, awarded to all participants in amounts of $2000, $1000, and $550.

title: About | Idea Forge
description: Idea Forge The Idea Forge is a prototyping facility focused on design and innovation. We are a flexible, cross-disciplinary collaborative space where students can imagine, design, create, and test products and solutions to meet a range of societal and customer needs.

title: Find Us | Idea Forge
description: Find Us | Idea Forge | University of Colorado Boulder Skip to main content Translate English Spanish Chinese French German Korean Lao Nepali Japanese Tibetan Search Enter the terms you wish to search for.

title: Drop-In Design Lab | Idea Forge
description: A true project work area, the Drop In Design Lab, affectionately known as the DIDL, begs for students to get in and get working on projects. The DIDL (MBE 178), the space holds a SolidWorks CAD/LabView/engineering software computer lab and plenty of project work space. There are two study rooms available for students to reserve - rooms 178A and 178B. Both have phones and full presentation capabilities. Borrow an external camera from Victoria (MBE 130G).

title: Chevron Design Studio | Idea Forge
description: The Chevron Design Studio is a large design and build space run by Design Center Colorado and dedicated to the Mechanical Engineering and Biomedical Engineering Senior Design classes. This course allows students to work on industry sponsored projects while guided by a faculty advisor. The course is a transitionary experience for students as they bridge from being a student to thinking like an engineer in industry. Design teams have dedicated work and storage space.

title: Northrop Grumman Think Tank | Idea Forge
description: The Think Tank is a conference room suspended over the Idea Forge Commons. Available to be reserved by anyone on campus, the room seats 8 people and has full projection capabilities. It is commonly used by students and faculty alike.

title: MESAB Teleconference Room | Idea Forge
description: The MESAB Teleconference Room (MBE 179) fulfills the need for a large meeting space (16 seats) with video conference capabilities on campus. Schedule the room for your class project or student group meeting. It is often used by students to meet with industry partners, faculty to hold research meetings, and student groups and startups. Bring your dry-erase markers to write on the white board table. This space has been named by the generous members of the Mechanical Engineering Strategic Advisory Board (MESAB).

title: Sheppard Electronics Lab | Idea Forge
description: The Sheppard Electronics Lab in the Idea Forge is your go-to place for all things electronics, from basic electronics to electrical systems, and circuitry design to PCB manufacture. With soldering irons, DAQ equipment, computers, and various workshops, the Sheppard Electronics Lab can help you create, test and manufacture your project.

title: Pretotyping Cabinet | Idea Forge
description: The Pretotyping Cabinet is your first stop for early prototyping needs. With cheap, expendible, easy-to-use materials in stock, you can make low resolution prototypes, answer your design questions, and develop your idea quickly and effectively.

title: Finishing Room | Idea Forge
description: The Finishing Room is a well ventilated room that is a great place for any dirty work: painting, staining, using epoxy, sanding, etc.

title: Checkout Office | Idea Forge
description: The Checkout Office has an assortment of fasteners, hardware (hand tools, snap rings, punches, etc.), components (springs, bearings, gears, belts, etc.), and test equipment (scales, force gauges, accelerometers, DAQ’s, cameras, etc.) for student to check out. There are also several large pieces of test equipment available for student use, including an optical comparator, Instron, Lansmont Shock Tester, and Rockwell Hardness Tester.

title: Q&A: Jon Rosenberg of Cold Case Gear - Startup Colorado
description: Necessity inspires innovation. Just look at Cold Case Gear, a Pagosa Springs startup that manufactures insulated, waterproof phone cases for backcountry adventures. After numerous electronic failures in extreme conditions, Jon Rosenberg and his wife Deirdre decided to build the toughest and most cold resistant cases on the market. Now, Cold Case Gear is launching their West Slope Thermal Phone Case, just in time for winter. We spoke with Jon about his experience launching an outdoor startup in rural Colorado. Startup Colorado: You launched Cold Case Gear after a successful Kickstarter campaign. What tips do you have for other businesses considering crowdfunding?Jon: Calculate every single cent that you need and tack on 20% for unforeseen expenses and various fees. Make sure that your product has a good enough margin that you can grow once you have fulfilled orders. It’s easy to run out of money AND product. You need great margins to truly launch your business off Kickstarter.

title: Q&A: Jon Rosenberg of Cold Case Gear - Startup Colorado
description: Necessity inspires innovation. Just look at Cold Case Gear, a Pagosa Springs startup that manufactures insulated, waterproof phone cases for backcountry adventures. After numerous electronic failures in extreme conditions, Jon Rosenberg and his wife Deirdre decided to build the toughest and most cold resistant cases on the market. Now, Cold Case Gear is launching their West Slope Thermal Phone Case, just in time for winter. We spoke with Jon about his experience launching an outdoor startup in rural Colorado. Startup Colorado: You launched Cold Case Gear after a successful Kickstarter campaign. What tips do you have for other businesses considering crowdfunding?Jon: Calculate every single cent that you need and tack on 20% for unforeseen expenses and various fees. Make sure that your product has a good enough margin that you can grow once you have fulfilled orders. It’s easy to run out of money AND product. You need great margins to truly launch your business off Kickstarter.

title: "Investment Crowdfunding: Anarchy in the U.K.?" by Andrew A. Schwartz
description:
Investment crowdfunding is a new type of venture capital market open to the broad public--'the crowd'--and the United States and United Kingdom adopted rather different legal regimes to govern and police it. In order to protect investors, the United States enacted an extensive set of laws and regulations, while the United Kingdom took a 'liberal' approach to investment crowdfunding, imposing few legal rules and relying primarily on private ordering.
A decade has now passed, allowing us to see whether the liberal U.K. market has devolved into anarchy and failure in the absence of heavy regulation. Recently published data reflects well on the liberal model: The U.K. has the largest and most successful investment crowdfunding market in the world by far, generating one billion dollars in startup finance each year with practically no fraud, and providing investors with competitive financial returns.

title: "Regional Venture Deals" by Paige L. Wilson
description: What might allow a region to suddenly excel at attracting venture capital funding, and what role do lawyers play in such a shift? The Midwest offers a useful case study because it has succeeded at increasing the size of its venture capital market by more than five hundred percent over the past decade. This Article is the first-ever empirical study to explore in depth the changing practices of the region. This Article begins by comparing startup lawyering practices in the Midwest to startup lawyering practices in the major innovation hubs on the coasts. Drawing upon lawyer interviews, industry reports, and data from actual deals, this novel study finds that early-stage venture capital deals in the Midwest contain more investor-friendly terms that seek to provide investors with greater control over company actions and higher returns on early exits. Study data suggest that these deal differences are attributable to (1) the nascency of the Midwest venture capital ecosystem, (2) market dynamics that favor investors, and (3) a regional culture that emphasizes careful growth. Despite these regional differences, the study also shows that startup lawyers are actively facilitating convergence between Midwest deal practices and coastal deal practices. This finding goes to an important question in the innovation literature regarding whether contracts should be tailored to local market conditions or whether they should conform to a one-size-fits-all model. This Article offers empirical evidence that nationalized contracts are crucial to fostering rapid growth in emerging startup ecosystems such as the Midwest. With its original dataset, this Article highlights the vital role that startup lawyers perform in boosting regional economic development.
